With no large domestic package dispatches scheduled this quarter, our performance rested 
largely on the equipment business. Order booking for large package orders have yet to pick up 
steam, though as we speak, some large packages are coming close to finalization. 
 
On a positive note, export sales have dramatically increased from INR31 crores last year to 
INR64 crores in the first half. We have seen moderate growth in order booking in this quarter, 
which is largely attributable to renewed demand coming from the CNG markets, and we 
expect this year to be a good one for this segment after a few years of fairly stagnant demand. 
 
We have also booked significant orders for our refrigeration equipment coming from the food 
processing space. Our focus on innovation continues. We filed more than 65 IP applications in 
the first half of FY27. While there were no new product launches this quarter, we are 
developing several new technologies and extending the range of recently launched products 
such as Khione and Tyche. 
 
Our subsidiary, Systems and Components had a muted half on the sales side with revenues of 
INR9 crores. However, its order book has grown from INR4.1 crores at the start of the year to 
INR22 crores today, which gives us confidence in its growth over the coming quarters. 
 
Now I will come to the individual businesses. Starting with the air compressor segment. This 
segment has had several bright spots this year. We have been seeing some good growth in 
segments like diesel portables and PET bottling compressors, which we have re-entered after a 
long time. 
 
These are in addition to some segments where we have traditionally been strong, such as CO2, 
cement, etc. We are also seeing traction in syngas compressors and have booked a few orders 
for these as well. 
 
Additionally, our newly launched Hydrino is seeing good traction in the pharmaceutical space. 
Coming to refrigeration. Like last year, our packaging business remains slow in the first half, 
while demand from food processing and cold storage has been quite strong. 
 
We've booked orders across all 3 product lines, Khione, KC/KCX and Tyche. Our ammonia 
reciprocating compressors remain the dominant machine in this space and saw strong traction 
this year as well. This was largely driven by the food processing industry. 
 
We are also continuing to build out the Zephyros range, and we have successfully 
commercialized it this quarter. Coming to process gas. This year looks to be a strong one for 
this business. After a slower start to the year, the demand for CNG compressors seems to be 
very strong with large orders being booked last quarter even in this quarter, the trend 
continues. 
 
The opportunity pipeline for gas system also looks strong, but order finalization is taking some 
time. We expect this to pick up in the current quarter. Last quarter, we also dispatched India's 
first 1,000 bar hydrogen refuelling station. It's a first of its kind installation and a clear 
demonstration of KPCL's capabilities in this segment.

Our tie-up with Kobe Compressors will broaden the range of products we can offer both 
existing and new customers. Under our current partnerships, we could not address certain 
downstream petrochemical markets requiring API 617 and API 618 compressors. We will now 
be able to compete there against what are largely imported packages. 
 
This partnership also gives us the ability to serve very large compressor requirements in the 
tens of megawatts across specialized applications in petrochemicals, green ammonia and steel, 
among others. 
 
Scaling this will take time as we build and demonstrate our capabilities, but it will build on 
KPCL's participation in India's energy transition. Under O&M, we are now managing more 
than 1,060 CNG stations at a pan-India level, adding 90 stations during the first half of FY27. 
 
Coming to the outlook for the second half of this year. The first half of this year was largely 
impacted by slower execution of orders from the Precision Engineering division than what was 
expected. 
 
We expect this to change, and I'm pleased to say that the first dispatches are ongoing as I 
speak. Dispatches have started in this quarter and will continue into the next one. In addition to 
this, the orders for our equipment business, especially the CNG and refrigeration products 
should allow us to more than catch up in the second half. 
 
Last year, since most orders were booked in Q4, we did not have much to dispatch in the first 
half in terms of packaging. Starting this quarter, that should change. We remain confident of 
delivering strong growth this year despite the quarter gone by. 
 
We expect a strong Q3 and an even stronger Q4, driven by dispatches of our precision 
engineering business, large packages and our standard equipment sales. Before I conclude the 
business update, I would like to take a moment to wish all of you a very Happy Diwali and 
prosperous New Year.

Material cost for Q2 FY27 was at 44.7% of sales compared to 52.1% of sales in the 
corresponding quarter of the previous year. For H1 FY27, material cost to sales was at 44.3%, 
while in H1 FY26 was at 50% of sales. There was a reduction in the material cost by 5.7%. 
This is due to the better product mix and efforts of our backward integration of manufacturing. 
 
Employee-related expenses rose to INR109 crores in H1 FY27, up from INR97.4 crores in H1 
FY26. This increase was primarily driven by headcount addition and operational expansion at 
Nashik plant, along with scaling up business activities at Saswad and Hadapsar facilities. 
Company remains debt-free, resulting into zero interest costs or borrowing-related expenses 
for both Q2 as well as H1 FY27. 
 
Depreciation increased by approximately INR3 crores in H1 FY27, primarily due to capital 
expenditure incurred on Nashik as well as Saswad plant in the previous year. Accordingly, 
depreciation charge during H1 FY27 stood at INR17.9 crores compared with INR14.9 crores 
in H1 FY26. 
 
The increase in manufacturing other expenses was primarily attributed to the full year impact 
of the operations at our Nashik plant and the higher activity levels in our service business. 
These expenses comprises of both fixed and variable costs and stood at INR149.3 crores in H1 
FY27 against INR133.5 crores in the corresponding period of the previous year.

INR64.8 crores at 16.8% margin in the corresponding quarter of the previous year. For the first 
half of the financial year H1 FY27, EBITDA was at INR103 crores with a margin of 16.2% 
against INR109 crores with 16.4% was recorded in H1 FY26.

12.1% for Q2 FY27 against INR56.9 crores in Q2 FY26 at the rate of 14.8%. PBT of INR85.1 
crores for H1 FY27, while PBT of INR93.8 crores in H1 FY26. 
 
Exceptional item and exceptional income of INR11 crores was recognized below the PBT line 
in Q2 and H1 due to surrender of 1.77 acres of land out of 160 acres of land in Nashik for state 
government's road infrastructure project.
